There is presently a race condition between the bonding periodic
link monitor and the updating of a slave's speed and duplex.  The former
occurs on a periodic basis
column2: and the latter in response to a driver's

column1: calling of netif_carrier_on.
It is possible for the periodic monitor to run between the
driver call of netif_carrier_on and the receipt of the NETDEV_CHANGE
event that causes bonding to update the slave's speed and duplex.  This
manifests most notably as a report that a slave is up and ""0 Mbps full
duplex"" after enslavement
column2: but in principle could report an incorrect

column1: speed and duplex after any link up event if the device comes up with a
different speed or duplex.  This affects the 802.3ad aggregator
selection
column2: as the speed and duplex are selection criteria.

column1: This is fixed by updating the speed and duplex in the periodic
monitor
This was done historically in bonding
bond_update_speed_duplex was removed in commit 876254ae2758 (""bonding:
don't call update_speed_duplex() under spinlocks"")
under lock.  Later
column2: the locking was changed to only hold RTNL

column1: after commit 876254ae2758 (""bonding: don't call update_speed_duplex()
under spinlocks"") this call is again safe.
